title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy NGC 3256
caption: Peculiar galaxy NGC 3256, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3256, VV 065, AM 1025-433 · constellation Vela · about 100 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Two long, luminous tails swirl out from the body of NGC 3256, and its central region is tangled with dark lanes of dust. The galaxy looks like a single, oddly shaped object, but it is the leftover of a collision between two separate galaxies that happened long ago.

The tails are the clearest clue to that past. Gravity pulled them out of the original galaxies during the encounter, and they are now studded with an unusually dense population of star clusters. Hidden in the dusty middle is a double nucleus.

NGC 3256 lies about 100 million light-years away in Vela, and NASA calls it a nearby template for studying the young star clusters that form in tidal tails. The galaxy belongs to the Hydra-Centaurus supercluster complex, an enormous grouping of galaxies. NASA notes that encounters of this kind play out over several hundred million years.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: The 35-minute exposure gathers far more light than the eye can.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image is one of 59 colliding-galaxy pictures released in April 2008 on its 18th launch anniversary. According to NASA, only about one nearby galaxy in a million is caught colliding today.
alt: A distorted galaxy with a dusty center and two long, bright tails curving outward.
